Physicochemical characterisation

Sequence-only descriptors for in-house binder designs

Modified

November 6, 2026

These are descriptors, not predictions. Nothing in this track is fitted, trained, or correlated against the experimental outcome columns. The experimental metadata travels alongside the descriptors so a human can look at both; no relationship between them is computed or implied. Several of these descriptors — the instability and aliphatic indices especially — are literature heuristics with weak, context-dependent relevance to recombinant expression in E. coli, and are not quality scores.

What this computes

Sequence-only properties for each binder (2026-11-05T0754Z_physchem_descriptors-10binders): length, molecular weight, pI, net charge at pH 7.0 and 8.0, GRAVY, instability and aliphatic indices, aromaticity with explicit F/W/Y counts, cysteine count and parity, the full 20-residue composition as percentages, charged fraction over DEKR, reduced and oxidised extinction coefficients at 280 nm, Shannon entropy of composition (base 2), longest run of AVILMFWYC, and the maximum mean Kyte-Doolittle hydropathy over a 9-residue window with its position.

65 columns, 20 rows: 10 binders x 2 construct forms. 0 sequences rejected on validation.

A structural tier (SASA, secondary structure, structure-corrected solubility) and an ESM2 embedding tier are planned as additional stages contributing their own columns to the same table. Neither is implemented. The embedding tier is blocked on a decision about its role.

Verification before use

The implementation was checked against independently known values before it was run on real sequences (2026-11-05T0749Z_physchem_smoketest): 66 checks, 0 failures.

Quantity Published (ProtParam) Computed Tolerance
Molecular weight 8564.84 Da 8564.7357 Da ±0.5
Isoelectric point 6.56 6.5616 ±0.2
Extinction at 280 nm 1490 M⁻¹cm⁻¹ 1490 M⁻¹cm⁻¹ exact

Reference protein: bovine-ubiquitin-P0CG53-1-76. Edge cases covered a 5-residue peptide, zero-cysteine and zero-aromatic sequences (extinction coefficient must be exactly 0), an all-alanine sequence, and rejection of sequences containing X or a hyphen. The pI tolerance is 0.2 pH units because Biopython’s pKa table differs slightly from the ExPASy web implementation.

Tag handling, and why there are two rows per binder

Purification tags and expression leaders change every number above, and this set mixes tagged and untagged constructs. Each binder therefore appears twice: as_given and tag_stripped. Stripping removes a terminal run of ≥ 6 H at either terminus, a leading [‘MGSS’, ‘MGS’, ‘M’] leader (longest match first), and a GS-rich linker of ≥ 3 residues only where directly adjacent to a removed tag. 7 of 10 binders had something removed.

MMP9B17 173 172 nterm_leader=M
MMP9B7 87 84 nterm_leader=MGS
MMP9B9 128 127 nterm_leader=M

This is not cosmetic. Stripping IL10NB1’s C-terminal His tag moves its pI from 6.63 to 5.09 — six histidines are a real titratable group near neutral pH. Cross-binder comparisons should use the tag_stripped rows; as_given describes the protein that was actually expressed.

It is a VH-linker-VH construct whose two domains are joined by GGGGS repeats; those are structural, not tags, and are retained (stripped_elements = none, length 268). The smoke test covers this case, along with a sequence whose own composition contains HH and an internal HHHHHH that is not a tag.

Which binders are unusual, and on what

  • MMP9B17 is the only basic construct (pI 9.28, net charge +7.8 at pH 7), the only one with substantial cysteine (6), and has the highest window hydropathy (2.41) and entropy (3.99 bits).
  • IL10NB1 and IL10NB5, the two nanobody-format constructs, sit apart from the designed helical binders on nearly everything: charged fraction 0.11–0.12 against 0.31–0.53 for the rest, and GRAVY closest to zero.
  • IL6P233 has the lowest aromaticity (0.0225) and an extinction coefficient of only 1490 M⁻¹cm⁻¹ — one tyrosine, no tryptophan. Practically: A280 will quantify it poorly.
  • MMP9B9 has an instability index of 84.8, nearly double the median of 45.4.
  • All 10 binders have an even cysteine count, and 7 have none at all. GRAVY is negative for every one, so all are net hydrophilic.

Descriptors against observed outcomes: a sanity check, not a result

This cannot be evidence. 10 binders, with 2 non-expressers, 3 pellet and 5 supernatant cases. No p-value or correlation coefficient against any outcome column has been computed, and none should be. What follows checks that the pipeline produces sane numbers and that the descriptors are not secretly encoding the answer.

pellet (insoluble) (n=3) supernatant (soluble) (n=5) no expression (n=2)
fraction_charged_DEKR 0.11 – 0.33 0.31 – 0.53 0.45 – 0.49
gravy -0.36 – -0.13 -1.25 – -0.39 -0.89 – -0.86
instability_index 37.79 – 46.52 44.33 – 84.76 28.11 – 38.33
longest_hydrophobic_run 7.00 – 7.00 3.00 – 6.00 2.00 – 3.00
length 84.00 – 268.00 90.00 – 172.00 89.00 – 105.00

The charged fraction and GRAVY ranges of the 3 pellet and 5 supernatant cases nearly touch but do not cleanly separate. Two of the three pellet cases are the nanobody-format IL10 constructs, which differ from the helical designs in format, length and origin — so the split is confounded with construct class, not just with these descriptors. The instability index runs opposite to the folklore, being lower in the insoluble group (37.8–46.5) than in the soluble one (44.3–84.8). None of this is a signal.

IL6P233 versus IL6AD15

These two share their C-terminal 30 residues (verified identical from the sequences in the output table: True) and differ across their N-terminal 60. IL6P233 did not express; IL6AD15 expressed and was mostly soluble. Both were tried at 37 °C, and the notes record no 30 °C attempt for IL6P233.

binder_id IL6P233 IL6AD15
length 90.0000 90.0000
molecular_weight 10393.5696 10599.8158
isoelectric_point 4.5420 4.5359
net_charge_pH7 -12.4371 -13.1787
net_charge_pH8 -13.0112 -13.9303
gravy -0.8633 -1.0178
instability_index 38.0167 55.8956
aliphatic_index 98.6667 93.2222
aromaticity 0.0222 0.0556
count_Y 1.0000 4.0000
ext_coeff_280_reduced 1490.0000 5960.0000
longest_hydrophobic_run 2.0000 3.0000
shannon_entropy_bits 3.3177 3.1940
fraction_charged_DEKR 0.4889 0.5222

They are near-identical on pI, net charge and hydropathy. The differences are small and mostly point the wrong way: the binder that failed to express has the lower instability index (38.0, under the conventional threshold of 40) and the higher aliphatic index (98.7 versus 93.2), while the one that expressed scores 55.9.

No computed descriptor here explains the difference in outcome. For a pipeline sanity check that is the useful answer: it says these descriptors are not covertly encoding the result, and it is consistent with the cause lying somewhere sequence-only descriptors cannot see — local folding, codon or mRNA effects, toxicity, or simply that only one induction temperature was tried.

## What this computes

```{python}
#| echo: false
Markdown(
    f"Sequence-only properties for each binder {lr.cite(CHAR, P)}: length, "
    f"molecular weight, pI, net charge at pH "
    f"{' and '.join(str(v) for v in p['net_charge_ph_values'])}, GRAVY, "
    f"instability and aliphatic indices, aromaticity with explicit F/W/Y "
    f"counts, cysteine count and parity, the full 20-residue composition as "
    f"percentages, charged fraction over {p['charged_residue_set']}, reduced "
    f"and oxidised extinction coefficients at 280 nm, Shannon entropy of "
    f"composition (base {p['entropy_log_base']}), longest run of "
    f"{p['hydrophobic_residue_set']}, and the maximum mean "
    f"{p['hydrophobicity_scale']} hydropathy over a "
    f"{p['sliding_window_residues']}-residue window with its position.\n\n"
    f"{len(props.columns)} columns, {len(props)} rows: "
    f"{p['binders']} binders x {props.construct_form.nunique()} construct "
    f"forms. {p['rejected']} sequences rejected on validation."
)
```

## Descriptors against observed outcomes: a sanity check, not a result

::: {.caveat}
**This cannot be evidence.** 10 binders, with 2 non-expressers, 3 pellet and 5
supernatant cases. No p-value or correlation coefficient against any outcome
column has been computed, and none should be. What follows checks that the
pipeline produces sane numbers and that the descriptors are not secretly
encoding the answer.
:::
